name: verify-in-runtime-not-by-reading
description: "In this Hammerspoon codebase, never declare something dead or correct from reading alone — probe the live runtime via `hs -c`"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory

Before calling code dead, or a fix correct, exercise it in the running Hammerspoon process
with `hs -c` and read the log. Reading the source is not evidence here.

**Why:** two failures in one session, both from reasoning instead of probing. `_whisper` looked
like dead state because its `recording` field was never written — it was actually the only GC
root keeping the trigger eventtap alive, and deleting it killed the trigger a few minutes after
every reload. And a unit test passed on a broken `triggerHeld` because the stub fed it a flag
word that `checkKeyboardModifiers` never actually returns.

**How to apply:** post synthetic events, force `collectgarbage("collect")`, read
`$TMPDIR/whisper-dictate/whisper-dictate.log` — the recipes are in AGENTS.md. When writing a
test with a stubbed API, first check what that API returns in the real runtime. See also
[[prefers-community-sources]].
